title: Preventing filter failure with differential pressure monitoring
summary: Differential pressure monitoring shows how filtration is performing and when a filter should be changed.
paragraphs: Differential pressure is one of the most important measurements in particulate filtration systems. It is the difference between inlet and outlet pressure across a filter housing and shows how much resistance the media is creating.

As contaminants load the media, resistance and differential pressure rise. Manufacturers publish recommended and maximum change-out pressures. Running a filter all the way to the maximum rating rarely doubles life, because after roughly 15–20 psi pressure often rises exponentially.

Operators can use two gauges, a dedicated differential gauge, or sensors tied to a PLC with alarms. A low clean start-up differential (often below 2 psi) indicates the system is sized correctly and leaves more usable life before change-out.
A sudden drop in differential without a flow change can signal media breakthrough. Steady monitoring protects downstream equipment and reduces unplanned downtime.
